hourly.summary: The forum buzzes with Manchester United transfer talk—JJ Gabriel's scholarship saga and a fresh bid for a Barcelona target—while data analysts warn of a brutal upcoming fixture run. Matchday pub plans for an away day provide light relief, but the overall mood is one of cautious anticipation: youth retention offers hope, yet the schedule looms large.

daily.summary: Sentiment plummeted dramatically across the day: early tribal toxicity (4/10) gave way to cautious transfer optimism (6/10) by midday, then collapsed into full-blown crisis (2/10) after a shocking 2-0 opening-day loss to newly promoted Hull City. The defeat — conceding both goals from set pieces — instantly erased pre-match hope, leaving fans questioning everything and nostalgic for past glory.

weekly.summary: The week began with fleeting schadenfreude over Manchester City's 115 charges but rapidly curdled into a sustained cycle of aggrieved grievance — fixated on INEOS ownership, institutional bias, and United's own injury crisis. A brief mid-week recovery fueled by the women's derby win and transfer optimism proved short-lived, as the period closed in grim resignation: toxic outrage at Zirkzee and the regime settling into gallows humor that masks a fanbase that has normalized mediocrity and a 13-year title drought.
